Closing verification (sanctioned non-force path), main @9bdb22f5887. Ticked all 3 ACs after independently re-verifying:

- AC1 (explicit user approval before any change): the implementation ticket c1bf-475a-5bbc-4976 (closed) states in its own description that it 'Implement[s] the approved "support both" SESSION_ID disposition (decided on 83f2, dull-strife-sigma)' — i.e. the approval was recorded on THIS ticket and preceded the change, and c1bf itself then passed the project's close gates. No autonomous change was made ahead of that decision.
- AC2 (decision recorded — keep ambient / rename / support both): SUPPORT BOTH, with the rebar-owned var taking precedence. Live in the code at src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py:37-41, whose _SESSION_ID_VARS tuple is (REBAR_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, OPENCODE_SESSION_ID, SESSION_ID) — the explicit rebar var first, ambient SESSION_ID last, so ambient pickup is preserved and the collision risk is answered by precedence rather than a rename.
- AC3 (if changed: alias + docs + tests): alias — REBAR_SESSION_ID, shipped in commit dec75f22fb ('feat(transition): REBAR_SESSION_ID precedence over ambient SESSION_ID (c1bf)'). Docs — docs/config.md:498-503 documents the full precedence chain, that it is additive with no deprecation warning, and why Codex is covered by a SessionStart shim rather than a native var. Tests — verified now: '.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py tests/unit/test_session_shims.py -q' -> 22 passed.

Note on links: I did NOT add a 'duplicates' link to c1bf. c1bf is not a duplicate of this ticket — it is the IMPLEMENTATION of the disposition this ticket decided. The existing relates_to link is the honest relation, so I left it as is.
